report.summary: Chunk 12 of 13 of containment.py: read-back of job limits, _HandleAllowlist class, and spawn_contained function definition.
risks: _HandleAllowlist.__init__ | medium | Raises ContainmentUnavailable for empty allowlist, but the error message says 'an empty allowlist is not a list' which is misleading; an empty list is a list. | Check if the behavior is intentional; if not, change message to 'allowlist must not be empty'.

spawn_contained | low | Docstring claims 'max_processes and max_job_memory_bytes TIGHTEN the job's caps and cannot loosen them' but the actual code for applying caps is not in this chunk; claim uncheckable. | Review the full function implementation.

spawn_contained | low | Docstring claims 'bInheritHandles is written as allowlist is not None' but the code for CreateProcess is not in this chunk; claim uncheckable. | Review the full function implementation.

handoff.purpose: Implements read-back validation of job limits, defines _HandleAllowlist for bounded handle inheritance, and starts spawn_contained function.

symbols.name: _HandleAllowlist
symbols.note: Manages PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST for bounded handle inheritance; holds reference to HANDLE array.

symbols.name: spawn_contained
symbols.note: Starts a process at Low integrity with job object containment; defined partially in this chunk.

claims.text: ``max_processes`` and ``max_job_memory_bytes`` TIGHTEN the job's caps and cannot loosen them: each is combined with the module ceiling by ``min()``, written as one expression so there is no state in which a caller asked for more and got it.
claims.why: The implementation of the cap combination is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Passing ``None`` -- what every production caller does -- gets :data:`JOB_ACTIVE_PROCESS_LIMIT` and :data:`JOB_MEMORY_LIMIT_BYTES`.
claims.why: The default values are not assigned in this chunk.

claims.text: HANDLE INHERITANCE IS BOUNDED, NOT CONFIGURABLE. There is no ``inherit`` parameter, no ``close_fds``, and no way to pass a raw handle: ``log`` is typed to :class:`LowIntegrityLog`, an object only this module can construct, on a target only this module labels, with rights only this module chooses.
claims.why: The function signature does not include inherit or close_fds; log is typed as LowIntegrityLog which is defined elsewhere in the module.

claims.text: ``bInheritHandles`` is written as ``allowlist is not None`` so inheritance and the allowlist can never disagree.
claims.why: The CreateProcess call is not in this chunk.

claims.text: With ``log=None`` no handle crosses at all and the child has no stdio; that is the original behaviour and remains the default.
claims.why: The handling of log=None is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Raises :class:`ContainmentUnavailable` on any platform or API failure, and never falls back to an ordinary spawn.
claims.why: The chunk shows ContainmentUnavailable being raised on various failures; no fallback is present.

claims.text: Holds a reference to the HANDLE array for its whole lifetime: ``UpdateProcThreadAttribute`` stores a POINTER to the value, so letting the array be collected before ``CreateProcessAsUserW`` would hand the kernel a dangling list -- and a dangling allowlist is an unbounded one.
claims.why: The class stores self._array as an instance variable, preventing garbage collection.

observations.what: Read-back of job limits: after setting limits, the code queries the job and validates that the limits were applied correctly, raising ContainmentUnavailable if not.
The _HandleAllowlist class manages a PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST; it initializes the attribute list, updates it with the handles array, and provides a pointer for use in CreateProcess.
The spawn_contained function signature includes optional parameters max_processes and max_job_memory_bytes with docstring claims about their behavior.
